title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Every megawatt of electricity entering an AI training cluster must be conditioned on the way in and extracted as heat on the way out.
epigraph.author: Data Center Engineering First Principle

web_blocks.html: Vertiv designs, manufactures, and services the critical electrical and thermal infrastructure that keeps data centers, telecom networks, and industrial facilities online [1]. In its Form 10-K, Vertiv organizes its business into three geographic reportable segments: Americas, Asia Pacific (APAC), and Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA) [1]. Within each region, revenue is disaggregated across two primary offering lines: Products and Services & Spares [1, 2]. Starting in 2024, Products combined the legacy Critical Infrastructure & Solutions and Integrated Rack Solutions lines [1, 2].

web_blocks.caption: Vertiv Geographic Segment Revenue & Operating Profit Mix (FY2025 Audited vs. 9M 2026 YTD)
web_blocks.takeaway: Americas generates over 62% of Vertiv's revenue and nearly three-quarters of segment operating profit, though EMEA and APAC margins expanded sharply through Q3 2026.

web_blocks.html: Across offerings, Products accounted for $8,390.6 million (82.0% of total net sales) in FY2025 [2]. That was up from $6,393.5 million in FY2024 and $5,406.1 million in FY2023 [2]. Services & Spares generated $1,839.3 million (18.0% of FY2025 net sales), growing steadily from $1,618.3 million in FY2024 and $1,457.1 million in FY2023 [2]. Product shipments surge during hyperscale build cycles [1, 11]. Meanwhile, the growing installed base of liquid-cooling loops and megawatt UPS trains feeds multi-year preventive maintenance, commissioning, and spares revenue [1, 11].
To see how Vertiv's equipment works in practice, consider three concrete end-to-end deployments across its core product and service lines:

1. Thermal Management & Liquid Cooling (CoolTera CDUs & Liebert Chillers): When a North American hyperscaler or neocloud operator deploys a 100+ kW per rack NVIDIA Blackwell GB200 or Vera Rubin cluster, air conditioning alone fails [9, 16]. Vertiv supplies the full thermal chain from roof to chip [10, 16]. Roof-mounted Liebert free-cooling chillers reject heat to the outside atmosphere [10, 16]. Indoors, Vertiv XDU/CoolTera Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) pump, filter, and regulate ultra-pure glycol-water coolant through manifolds directly to server cold plates [10, 16]. Vertiv's engineering team co-designs the facility thermal loop and delivers factory-tested skids [11, 16]. PurgeRite technicians then mechanically flush, air-purge, and chemically stabilize the closed-loop piping before a single GPU powers on [11, 16]. Hardware is priced on an engineered project contract, usually paired with a 3-to-5-year preventive maintenance and fluid-hygiene service agreement [1, 11].

2. Critical Power Management (Trinergy UPS, Switchgear & Busways): AI training clusters draw massive, rapidly fluctuating electrical loads that can destabilize utility feeds [17]. For a multi-megawatt colocation campus in Virginia or Europe, Vertiv supplies medium-voltage switchgear, busway power distribution, and modular Trinergy UPS units [17]. These systems are engineered to ride through grid sags without dropping compute jobs [17]. Regional factories pre-integrate the units before Vertiv field engineers commission them on site [1, 17]. Customers also sign multi-year battery monitoring, thermal imaging, and 4-hour emergency SLA service contracts [1, 17].

3. Integrated Rack Solutions & Vertiv 360AI / OneCore: Enterprise and edge AI buyers, such as financial institutions or regional hospitals, often lack hyperscale internal engineering teams [18]. Vertiv packages Great Lakes heavy-duty racks, in-row cooling, rack PDUs, and Waylay predictive monitoring software into Vertiv 360AI or SmartRow reference architectures [12, 13, 18]. At larger scale, it offers prefabricated Vertiv OneCore modular blocks for Vera Rubin DSX [16, 18]. The customer buys one validated SKU bundle with predictable lead times [1, 18]. Vertiv technicians perform turnkey installation and ongoing remote diagnostics [1, 18].

web_blocks.caption: Vertiv Offering Mix Evolution (FY2023–FY2025 Audited)
web_blocks.takeaway: Product sales grew at nearly double the rate of services between 2023 and 2025 due to greenfield AI buildouts, creating a massive installed base for future high-margin service attach.

web_blocks.html: This mix shift carries a clear strategic payoff. Heavy product shipments compressed services from 21.2% of sales in 2023 to 18.0% in 2025 [2, 19]. Yet every gigawatt of Trinergy UPS and CoolTera CDU gear installed today expands the captive base for Vertiv's ~5,000 field service engineers [2, 19].

Geographically, Americas anchored Vertiv's FY2025 revenue of $10,229.9 million with $6,386.3 million (62.4% share) [1]. Asia Pacific contributed $2,019.2 million (19.7%), and EMEA added $1,824.4 million (17.8%) [1]. Americas concentration reflects US hyperscale AI cluster construction across Virginia, Texas, Ohio, and the Pacific Northwest [1, 8]. APAC captures semiconductor-adjacent deployments in Taiwan, Japan, Singapore, and India [1, 8]. EMEA reflects sovereign cloud and colocation expansion delayed earlier by European grid-permitting bottlenecks [1, 8].

book_paragraphs: To understand what Vertiv actually sells, imagine walking onto the construction floor of a 100-megawatt AI data center in Northern Virginia. Two physical problems dominate every square foot of that building: how to deliver massive amounts of clean, uninterrupted electricity to thousands of silicon chips, and how to strip away the colossal heat those chips generate before they melt or throttle. Vertiv sits on both sides of that equation.

In its financial statements, Vertiv organizes itself into three geographic regions—the Americas, Asia Pacific, and Europe, Middle East, and Africa—and splits its revenue into Products and Services & Spares. In 2025, the Americas generated 6.39 billion dollars, or 62.4 percent of total revenue, and delivered a remarkable 26.8 percent segment operating margin. Asia Pacific contributed 2.02 billion dollars at an 11.0 percent margin, while EMEA added 1.82 billion dollars at a 20.7 percent margin. By the third quarter of 2026, all three regions were expanding rapidly, with Americas hitting a 29.4 percent adjusted margin and EMEA jumping to 28.0 percent.

book_subsections.title: Walking the Thermal and Power Chains
paragraphs: Let us trace a concrete thermal example first. When a hyperscaler builds a cluster using NVIDIA Blackwell or Vera Rubin racks that pull over 100 kilowatts per cabinet, blowing cold air through perforated floor tiles no longer works. Vertiv steps in with an end-to-end liquid cooling chain. Outside the hall, Liebert chillers reject heat into the ambient air. Inside, CoolTera Coolant Distribution Units pump purified coolant through stainless-steel manifolds directly to cold plates sitting atop the GPUs. Before those GPUs are ever switched on, technicians from PurgeRite—the specialist Vertiv acquired for roughly a billion dollars in late 2025—flush, air-purge, and filter every inch of pipe so microscopic debris never clogs a million-dollar server.

Now walk over to the electrical room. AI training jobs create violent power swings as thousands of GPUs ramp from idle to full load in milliseconds. Vertiv supplies medium-voltage switchgear, busways, and its flagship Trinergy modular UPS systems to smooth out those transients and bridge utility outages. The customer pays a project-engineered price for the power train and typically attaches a multi-year service contract guaranteeing four-hour emergency response.

Finally, consider the enterprise or neocloud buyer who lacks an internal team of fifty data center architects. For them, Vertiv bundles Great Lakes server cabinets, power distribution, in-row cooling, and Waylay predictive monitoring software into pre-engineered blocks called Vertiv 360AI or prefabricated OneCore modules. Instead of coordinating six different vendors, the buyer orders one tested architecture.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Because product shipments exploded by nearly 25 percent annually from 2023 to 2025, Services & Spares dipped from 21.2 percent of revenue to 18.0 percent. Do not misread that as service weakness. Every CDU and UPS bolted to a data center floor today is a recurring maintenance contract waiting to activate over the next decade.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through a 120-Kilowatt AI Rack Deployment
paragraphs: To make Vertiv's product portfolio concrete, picture a hyperscale cloud provider building a new 100-megawatt AI training campus in Northern Virginia. Each server rack inside that hall packs dozens of high-wattage graphics processors drawing 100 to 130 kilowatts—roughly ten times the heat density of a traditional cloud rack. Blowing chilled air across those chips no longer works; the air cannot carry heat away fast enough before the silicon throttles.

Here is where Vertiv enters at every layer of the gray space and white space. On the power side, utility power arrives at medium voltage and steps down through Vertiv switchgear, busways, and Trinergy high-efficiency uninterruptible power supplies that protect the GPUs from millisecond grid sags. On the thermal side, chilled water circulates from outdoor free-cooling chillers into Vertiv's CoolTera-engineered coolant distribution units, which pump dielectric or treated water directly through manifolds and cold plates mounted on top of the chips.

Finally, Vertiv's ~5,000 field service engineers commission the entire thermal-electrical loop on site, test failover under full load, and stay attached on multi-year preventive maintenance contracts that generate recurring, high-margin service revenue long after the initial construction check clears.

book_subsections.title: Services & Spares: The Quiet Annuity Behind the Hardware
paragraphs: Hardware shipments grab the headlines whenever a hyperscaler announces a new gigawatt campus, yet Vertiv's Services and Spares business—$1,839.3 million, or 18.0 percent of FY2025 revenue—is what gives the franchise its durability. Every megawatt of switchgear, UPS capacity, and liquid-cooling plumbing commissioned today requires annual preventive maintenance, thermal-fluid monitoring, battery replacement, and emergency 24/7 response over a ten-to-fifteen-year equipment life.

Think about how that changes the economics of a data hall. A cloud operator might negotiate fiercely on the upfront price of a chiller or rack busway, but once the facility is live and hosting paying AI workloads, uptime becomes priceless. A single four-hour cooling outage can damage millions of dollars of silicon and breach customer service-level agreements. That is why Vertiv's field technicians—stationed across roughly 320 service centers globally—command high renewal rates and carry structurally higher gross margins than initial equipment sales.

book_subsections.title: Why Regional Mix Matters: Americas Speed vs. EMEA Permitting
paragraphs: Looking at Vertiv's geographic footprint—62.4 percent Americas, 19.7 percent Asia Pacific, and 17.8 percent EMEA—tells you where physical AI capacity is actually being energized. North American utilities and hyperscalers have moved fastest to sign multi-hundred-megawatt power purchase agreements and erect prefabricated data halls in Virginia, Ohio, and Texas.

By contrast, Europe has faced tighter municipal grid-connection queues and environmental permitting rules, which delayed some EMEA deployments into late 2026 and 2027. That geographic stagger is actually helpful for Vertiv's factories: as North American growth matures from triple-digit surges, pent-up EMEA and APAC sovereign-cloud builds provide a secondary wave of demand.

book_subsections.title: How Great Lakes and PurgeRite Fit the Puzzle
paragraphs: Vertiv's recent acquisitions are not random empire-building; each fills a physical gap in the high-density rack loop. Buying CoolTera in December 2023 gave Vertiv proprietary coolant distribution unit engineering right before liquid cooling went mainstream. Buying Great Lakes Data Racks and Cabinets in August 2025 for roughly $200 million expanded Vertiv's custom rack and enclosure capacity.

Most recently, acquiring PurgeRite for roughly $1.0 billion in December 2025 gave Vertiv specialized ultra-pure fluid flushing and commissioning capability—solving the exact operational headache that stalls hyperscale liquid-cooling turn-ups.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Vertiv's real edge is not a single gadget; it is the integration of the electrical room, the chiller yard, and the liquid manifold inside the white space, backed by engineers who know how to keep them running.
